reference_language_briefs.name: terrain loop edge
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: A long continuous mass bends to hold a shared edge and soften the boundary between dwelling and landscape.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Keep one unbroken perimeter line that curves around communal space while thickening at public touchpoints.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: Continuous frontage concentrates access and lets multiple units borrow light, outlook, and spill-out from the same loop.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Treat the ground as a public seam: one side stays open and porous, the other side gathers support and entry.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid segmented wings, isolated towers, and any literal site outline copying.

reference_language_briefs.name: cut court spine
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: A compact volume is hollowed to form a shared interior court that organizes family and neighbor life.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Carve one primary void through the mass and let rooms face inward to that protected center.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: The void increases usable social area without inflating bulk, concentrating adjacency around the court.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Anchor the building to the ground with a sheltered threshold that mediates street-to-court transition.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid decorative atriums, detached patios, and copying courtyard proportions from the image.

reference_language_briefs.name: linked ridge frame
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: Two or more occupiable bars interlock across an opening to form a shared raised connector.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Separate primary volumes, then bridge them so circulation and common programs occupy the joining zone.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: Interlocking adds cross-program contact and creates extra shared floor area above the gap.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Leave the lower level open enough for passage, landscape, or civic spill-out beneath the link.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid simple skybridges, symmetric twin blocks, and any copied span length or support spacing.

reference_language_briefs.name: hinged roof section
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: The mass folds along a section line so roof, wall, and circulation become one continuous inhabited slope.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Use a single sectional break that turns enclosure into a walkable thickness rather than stacked flat floors.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: The fold creates alternating high and low rooms, giving the section more usable variety without extra footprint.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Let the folded edge meet the site lightly, preserving a clear base zone for entry and shared outdoor use.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid generic peaked roofs, repeated gables, and facade-only folding.

reference_language_briefs.name: porous settlement field
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: Small masses gather as a loose field around shared pockets, producing a neighborhood-like grain.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Distribute units as a cluster with gaps that remain as usable courtyards, passages, and social slots.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: The field allows incremental growth and mixed unit sizes while keeping each cluster visually and socially legible.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Keep the ground permeable between clusters so movement and planting thread through the settlement.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid rigid grids, isolated objects, and uniform repetition without spatial breaks.

reference_language_briefs.name: courtyard weave field
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: A set of low masses weaves around several shared courts, balancing privacy with collective life.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Cluster around multiple voids rather than one dominant center so each group gets a distinct threshold.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: Multiple courts distribute activity, enabling staggered occupancy and smaller communities within the whole.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Let circulation weave at grade between masses so the open space feels continuous and inhabitable.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid monolithic bars and single-court compositions that collapse the field into one block.

reference_language_briefs.name: terraced plate stack
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: Occupiable floor plates step upward in a continuous sectional rhythm, making each level a usable terrace.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Use one stepping rule through the section so every rise becomes both structure and inhabited outdoor edge.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: Stepped plates multiply usable exterior room and allow each level to support housing, work, or shared program.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Hold the lower step open and civic, so the building rises while preserving a public base.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid decorative setbacks, pure ziggurat silhouettes, and non-occupiable tiers.

reference_language_briefs.name: rampede landscape stack
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: The section climbs as a continuous inhabited incline, joining floors into a walkable landscape.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Let each successive plate shift upward while remaining linked by a continuous sectional walk or terrace chain.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: The incline expands usable edge conditions and supports layered housing with shared access and outlook.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Keep the first level porous and generous so the stepped form reads as an extension of the site.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid isolated stair cores and simple stacked slabs without sectional continuity.

reference_language_briefs.name: civic threshold slab
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: A low public base supports a more private mass above, combining neighborhood address with everyday collective use.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Separate public and domestic bands in section, with the civic band tied directly to the ground plane.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: The lifted upper mass frees the ground for gathering, making the project feel denser in use than in footprint.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Treat the base as an urban room that can absorb waiting, entry, and shared activity.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid sealed podiums, blank plinths, and purely monumental bases.

reference_language_briefs.name: porous civic bar
reference_language_briefs.dominant_gesture: A linear building is punctured and offset to host public passages, shared rooms, and neighborhood-facing edges.
reference_language_briefs.spatial_rule: Keep the bar continuous enough to read as an institution, but open it with voids that invite cross-use.
reference_language_briefs.capacity_strategy: Notches and offsets create extra communal frontage and make the building work as both housing and civic interface.
reference_language_briefs.ground_strategy: Keep crossings and entries at grade so the bar behaves like part of the street network.
reference_language_briefs.avoid: Avoid rigid corridor blocks, fortress edges, and uniform bands with no public interruption.
